title: CSP allows unsafe-inline for scripts and styles
description: Content-Security-Policy header includes 'unsafe-inline' in both script-src and style-src directives, weakening XSS mitigation. Script-src also allows cdn.tailwindcss.com.
risks: If any user input is reflected without encoding, XSS attacks can bypass CSP due to unsafe-inline allowance.
attack_vectors: Identify any reflected input on blog or contact forms and inject inline JavaScript — CSP will not block it due to unsafe-inline.
remediation: Remove 'unsafe-inline' from script-src and style-src; use nonces or hashes for inline scripts and styles.

title: Sensitive files (.git, .env) return 403 — exist on server
description: .git/HEAD, .git/config, and .env all return HTTP 403 Forbidden, confirming these paths exist but are access-controlled by nginx.
risks: If access control is misconfigured or bypassed, source code or environment secrets could be leaked.
attack_vectors: Attempt path traversal, case variation, URL encoding, or alternative git endpoints (.git/logs/HEAD, .git/index) to bypass 403.
proof_of_existence: 403 162 — .git/HEAD returns 403 with 162 bytes body. Same for .git/config and .env.
remediation: Ensure nginx denies all dotfiles at server level; verify no path traversal bypasses exist.

title: Server version disclosure in HTTP headers
description: Server header reveals 'nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu)', providing version info useful for targeted CVE exploitation.
risks: Attackers can match version to known CVEs; nginx 1.24.0 needs CVE review by Bloodhound.
attack_vectors: Use disclosed version to identify applicable CVEs and craft targeted exploits.
proof_of_existence: Server: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) in HTTP response headers.
remediation: Set server_tokens off in nginx config and remove Ubuntu from server signature.

title: Author name disclosed in blog HTML meta tags
description: Blog page HTML meta author tag reveals 'Ahmed Chiboub' — useful for OSINT and social engineering.
risks: Attacker can use real employee name for phishing, credential stuffing, or social engineering campaigns.
attack_vectors: Search for Ahmed Chiboub on LinkedIn/GitHub for email patterns, credentials, or additional attack surface.
proof_of_existence: <meta name="author" content="Ahmed Chiboub"> in /blog/ page HTML.
remediation: Remove personal names from meta tags; use company name instead.

title: Form data submitted to third-party formspree.io
description: CSP form-action and connect-src allow formspree.io, indicating contact form data is sent to a third-party service.
risks: User-submitted form data (potentially PII) is processed by formspree.io — a third-party SaaS outside client control.
attack_vectors: If formspree.io account is compromised, attacker could intercept or manipulate form submissions.
remediation: Self-host form processing endpoint; ensure data processing agreement with any third-party form service.

title: robots.txt fully open allowing all crawlers
description: robots.txt allows all user agents with no Disallow directives; references sitemap.xml.
risks: All content is indexable by search engines; sensitive paths if later discovered would be crawled.
attack_vectors: Review sitemap.xml for undiscovered URLs and content paths.
remediation: Add Disallow directives for sensitive or non-public paths.

title: Host header injection not exploitable
description: Server returns identical content (18860 bytes) regardless of Host header value (admin.cyberian-defenses.com, test.cyberian-defenses.com).
risks: No host header injection risk identified; server does not use Host header for routing.
proof_of_existence: HTTP/1.1 200 OK, Content-Length: 18860 for both admin.cyberian-defenses.com and test.cyberian-defenses.com Host headers.
remediation: No action needed; continue to reject unknown Host headers as defense-in-depth.

title: X-Original-URL/X-Rewrite-URL header bypass not effective
description: Sending X-Original-URL: /admin and X-Rewrite-URL: /admin headers returns homepage (200), not admin page — no auth bypass via header manipulation.
risks: No auth bypass risk identified via these headers.
attack_vectors: N/A — tested and not exploitable on nginx.
proof_of_existence: HTTP/1.1 200 OK, Content-Length: 18860 — same homepage returned, no route change.
remediation: No action needed; these headers are IIS-specific and don't affect nginx.

title: Nuclei vulnerability scanning incomplete — templates missing
description: Multiple Nuclei template directories were empty or missing, preventing automated vulnerability scanning.
risks: CVE-based and injection vulnerabilities may remain undetected without template-based scanning.
attack_vectors: N/A — tooling gap, not a vulnerability.
proof_of_existence: FTL: Could not run nuclei: no templates provided for scan (multiple template paths returned same error).
remediation: Install/update nuclei templates with 'nuclei -update-templates' before next scan cycle.

title: Blog section is primary attack surface for content injection
description: /blog/ returns 200 (34749 bytes) with dynamic content, meta tags, and structured data — likely the primary surface for XSS or content injection testing.
risks: If blog accepts user comments or has search/filter parameters, XSS or SQLi may be possible.
attack_vectors: Enumerate blog posts from sitemap.xml; test URL parameters, search forms, and comment sections for XSS and SQLi.
proof_of_existence: /blog/ returns HTTP 200 with 34749 bytes; sitemap.xml returns 200 with 1305 bytes containing blog post URLs.
remediation: Ensure all blog inputs are properly sanitized and encoded; implement CSP nonces.
